title: Migrations (advanced)
summary: Evolving a live schema safely: versioned migrations instead of create_all / db push.
body:
Evolving a live schema safely: versioned migrations instead of create_all / db push.

Why it matters: create_all and db push are great for labs. In production the schema changes while data exists — you need ordered, reviewed, repeatable migration files.

SQL ↔ ORM: Python: alembic revision --autogenerate + alembic upgrade head. Node: prisma migrate dev / migrate deploy. SQL: numbered .sql files applied in order.
why: create_all and db push are great for labs. In production the schema changes while data exists — you need ordered, reviewed, repeatable migration files.
objectives: Know why create_all never alters tables.
pitfalls: Adding NOT NULL without a default to a full table.
mappingNotes: Python: alembic revision --autogenerate + alembic upgrade head. Node: prisma migrate dev / migrate deploy. SQL: numbered .sql files applied in order.
teachAlong: Cause: Evolving a live schema safely: versioned migrations instead of create_all / db push.
Effect: run the exercise and read the gate's rule ids.

example.code:
alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add bio"
alembic upgrade head
example.sql: ALTER TABLE lab_authors ADD COLUMN bio TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '';

exercise.prompt: Answer every question — each wrong option explains why it is wrong.

questions.prompt: Your app is live. You add a column to a model. Why is Base.metadata.create_all() not enough?

options.text: create_all only creates missing tables — it never ALTERs an existing one
It drops and recreates the table, losing data
options.why: It is the opposite: create_all skips tables that exist, so the new column is never added.
It does nothing for existing tables — use Alembic (Python) or prisma migrate (Node).

questions.prompt: Which command creates a versioned migration file you commit to git?

options.why: db push syncs the schema without a migration history — fine for prototypes, not for production.

options.text: prisma migrate dev --name add_bio (or alembic revision --autogenerate)

options.why: generate only regenerates the TypeScript client; it does not touch the database.

questions.prompt: You add a NOT NULL column to a table that already has rows. What must the migration do?

options.text: Provide a DEFAULT or backfill existing rows before setting NOT NULL
Nothing — Postgres fills it with NULL
options.why: NULL violates NOT NULL, so ALTER TABLE fails on a non-empty table.
That loses production data; add a default or backfill instead.
